RADIOGRAPHIC EXAMINATION OF THE CHEST: 3/28/02
 
CLINICAL HISTORY: 60 years of age, Female, S/p lung transplant.

FINDINGS:
 
Sternotomy wires again noted, with a fracture of the inferior most 
wire. 
 
Interval development of a lobulated opacity extending posteriorly 
from the inferior aspect of the sternum in the anterior mediastinum, 
at the level of the broken sternotomy wire. The left pleural effusion 
has resolved. The lungs are clear. The heart is not enlarged. No 
edema. No significant bony abnormalities.
 
IMPRESSION:
 
1.  New versus enlarging opacity in the anterior mediastinum 
extending posteriorly from the inferior most sternotomy wire, best 
seen on lateral view. Clinical correlation for evidence of infection 
or inflammation may be helpful, and consider CT if clinically 
warranted, or a follow-up chest x-ray in 2 weeks.
2.  Resolved left pleural effusion.

There appears to have been interval repositioning of right pigtail 
pleural catheter.
 
Unchanged appearance of the lungs, with persistent apical density on 
the right likely indicating pleural scar. Pleural retraction noted on 
prior film appears to have resolved. No pleural effusion or 
pneumothorax. No cardiomegaly.
 
There is a small lucency over the right humeral midshaft, which 
appears to be surrounded by well corticated bone.
 
Repeat single view of chest at 11:10 hours demonstrates interval 
removal of right pigtail pleural drain. There is a small amount of 
pleural retraction over the right lateral chest wall, that may 
represent a small pneumothorax. However, there is no clear evidence 
of pneumothorax or pneumomediastinum.
 
IMPRESSION:
 
1.  Interval resolution of right paramediastinal pneumothorax, 
otherwise no significant interval change.
2.  Well corticated lucency over the right humeral midshaft. Although 
this does not appear to be an aggressive bony lesion, cannot rule out 
malignant etiologies such as multiple myeloma or metastatic disease. 
Recommend further workup at discretion of primary team.

report:
NARRATIVE:
RADIOGRAPHIC EXAMINATION OF THE CHEST: NOVEMBER 2015
 
CLINICAL HISTORY: 69 years of age, Male, Surveillance for metastatic 
cutaneous SCC.
 
COMPARISON: 11-13-15
 
PROCEDURE COMMENTS: Two views of the chest. 
 
FINDINGS:
 
Redemonstration of chain sutures and scarring in the right mid and 
lower lung zones. Nodular lesion measuring approximately 1.5 cm is 
noted in the right lung. Questionable masslike opacity is also noted 
at the inferior margin of the chain suture. Increased size of the 
right pleural effusion and unchanged size of the left pleural 
effusion. Linear opacities in the left midlung zone, likely 
representing atelectasis. 
 
Heart size is unchanged. Calcifications are again noted in the 
thoracic aorta. No acute osseous abnormalities. Surgical clips are 
present in the left supraclavicular region.
 
IMPRESSION:
 
1.  Nodular lesions in the right lung, concerning for possible 
metastasis. Recommend CT chest further evaluation.
 
2.  Increased right-sided pleural effusion and unchanged left pleural 
effusion.
 
3.  Linear opacities in the left midlung zone, likely representing 
atelectasis.

opacity with the tail pointing toward the hilum in the right lower 
lobe creates an unusual interface with either the posterior segment 
of the right upper lobe or superior segment of the right lower lobe.

overlying this area are multiple rib deformities compatible with old 
fracture. On the lateral view, there is blunting of the right

degenerative changes of the spine are present.

toward the hilum could represent pneumonia, however a mass is not 
excluded. Alternatively, pregnant findings could be related to old 
fracture deformities of the overlying ribs. Recommend further 
evaluation with chest CT.

or scarring with adjacent lower lobe opacities, right greater than 
left, which may reflect atelectasis, consolidation, or scarring 
compared to 5/28/05.

RADIOGRAPHIC EXAMINATION OF THE CHEST: 5/26/2013
 
CLINICAL HISTORY: 40 years of age, Female, S/p surgical resection of 
a right carcinoid tumor.
 
COMPARISON: 13 26th May
 
PROCEDURE COMMENTS: Two views of the chest. 
 
FINDINGS:
 
Postsurgical changes of the right hemithorax are again demonstrated 
with several suture lines in the right upper lung zone and slightly 
increased right pleural thickening and/or loculated pleural effusion 
which persists along the lateral aspect of the hemithorax. Resolved 
right sided subcutaneous emphysema. Again noted is evidence of volume 
loss in the right hemithorax with eventration of the right hemithorax 
and elevation of the right bronchus. There is improved aeration of 
the left hemithorax with improved atelectasis of the base. Stable 14 
mm nodule in the left upper lung zone. Within limitations of 
background abnormality, there is no acute cardiopulmonary process.
 
The cardiomediastinal silhouette is stable in configuration with 
similar right-sided hilar and mediastinal prominence. Pulmonary 
vascularity is unchanged.
 
No acute osseous abnormalities. Degenerative changes of the spine. 
Decreased gaseous distention of the stomach.
 
 
 
IMPRESSION:
 
1.  Postsurgical changes of the right hemithorax with slightly 
increased right pleural thickening and/or loculated pleural effusion 
in addition to volume loss. Within limitations of background 
abnormality, there is no acute cardiopulmonary process.
 
2.  Improved aeration of left hemithorax. Stable 14 mm nodule in the 
left upper lung zone.

NARRATIVE:
SINGLE UPRIGHT VIEW OF THE CHEST:  11-7-2014 
 
CLINICAL HISTORY:  A 97 year old man status post lung biopsy 
complicated by pneumothorax.  Followup pneumothorax.  
 
EXAM:  AP upright view of the chest:  11/07 at 1540 hours. 
 
COMPARISON:  11-7-14 at 1300 hours. 
 
FINDINGS:  Limited AP upright view of the chest demonstrates a stable 
left pneumothorax.  Redemonstration of a left upper lobe mass which 
abuts the mediastinum and the borders of which are ill-defined.  
There is opacity in the lung parenchyma adjacent to the mass lesion 
which may be atelectasis; however, superimposed infection cannot be 
excluded.  In addition, there is a retrocardiac air space opacity 
which may be atelectasis versus infection.  Probable left pleural 
effusion.  The right lung remains clear; however, there are 
increasing interstitial markings which may be related to low lung

pleural effusion with associated right basilar opacity.  Fluid tracts 
into the minor fissure.  Other than the basilar opacity, the right 
lung is clear.  There is mild apical pleuroparenchymal thickening 
noted at the right lung apex.  The left lung is clear with the 
exception of a nodular opacity noted at the left lung base, which may 
correspond to a nipple shadow; however, a discrete pulmonary nodule 
cannot be excluded.  Cardiomediastinal silhouette is stable in 
comparison to the prior examination; however, the right cardiac 
border is obscured by the right pleural effusion.  Tortuosity of the 
descending thoracic aorta is noted.  Regional osseous structures 
demonstrate mild degenerative changes of the spine.
 
 IMPRESSION: 
 
 1.  REDEMONSTRATION OF SMALL RIGHT PLEURAL EFFUSION WITH ASSOCIATED 
RIGHT BASILAR OPACITY.
 
 2.  NODULAR DENSITY PROJECTING AT THE LEFT LUNG BASE MEASURING 
APPROXIMATELY 5 MM, WHICH MAY REPRESENT THE PATIENT'S LEFT NIPPLE 
SHADOW.  HOWEVER, DISCRETE PULMONARY NODULE CANNOT BE EXCLUDED.  
RECOMMEND SHORT INTERVAL FOLLOW-UP EXAMINATION WITH PLACEMENT OF 
NIPPLE MARKERS ON FOLLOW-UP EXAMINATION.
 
 SUMMARY:4-POSSIBLY SIGNIFICANT FINDING; MAY NEED ACTION.

demonstrates interval placement of 3 right-sided chest tubes with 
partial reexpansion of the right upper and right middle lobes which 
were partially collapsed on the comparison film.  The previously 
demonstrated hydro-pneumothorax is much smaller status post chest 
tube placement with no clear fluid level seen at the right lung base. 
There is no mediastinal shift.  There is also a new left chest tube 
with no definite pneumothorax seen on the left side. There is a new 
endotracheal tube which is approximately 3.1 cm above the carina.  A 
nasogastric tube has also been placed with its tip in the very 
proximal stomach and its distal side port in the distal esophagus.  
There is a new epidural catheter in place.  There is also a new right 
internal jugular central venous catheter with its tip in the proximal 
superior vena cava.  There is a new patchy opacity throughout the 
right lung which likely represents atelectasis though could also be 
due to consolidation or postoperative contusion.  There is also 
increased opacity in the left lung base in the retrocardiac region.  
Lung volumes are lower when compared to the preoperative film.  
Postsurgical changes with clips projecting over the superior 
mediastinum are seen.
 
A second frontal chest x-ray from 6-14-20 at 3:53 a.m. 
demonstrates stable positioning of lines, tubes, and medical support 
devices with the exception of the endotracheal tube which is more 
proximal in position now 7.9 centimeters above the carina.  The 
nasogastric tube remains in the very proximal stomach with its distal 
side port in the distal esophagus.  The right pneumothorax is 
decreased in side no there is opacity at the right lung base 
suggesting reaccumulation of pleural fluid likely with atelectasis 
though underlying infection is also a possibility.  There is improved 
aeration at the left lung base with some slight remaining streaky 
opacity in the retrocardiac region.
 
IMPRESSION:
 
1.POSTOPERATIVE CHANGES TO THE MEDIASTINUM AS DESCRIBED ABOVE.
 
2.ENDOTRACHEAL TUBE 7.9 CM ABOVE THE CARINA.
 
3.NASOGASTRIC TUBE WITH SIDE-PORT IN THE DISTAL ESOPHAGUS AND TIP IN

small pleural effusion with increased associated opacity in the right 
lung base. There appears to be an interval development of 
superimposed pulmonary edema.

1.  Postoperative changes from aVR. Lung volumes are low with left 
greater than right small-to-moderate pleural effusions and associated 
left greater than right lung base opacities.
 
2.  Superimposed interstitial pulmonary edema.
 
3.  Large hiatal hernia.

apical pleural thickening is noted.

cardiomegaly.

pleural thickening versus small pleural effusions. Right apical 
pleural thickening is noted.
 
3.  No focal consolidation.

CLINICAL HISTORY: 17 years of age, Male, known history of cystic fibrosis, evaluate pleural effusion

PROCEDURE COMMENTS: Single view of the chest. 
 
FINDINGS:
Stable position of right upper extremity PICC line terminating 2.9 cm below level of the carina in the distal SVC. Slight interval retraction of left basilar pigtail catheter.
 
Reticulonodular opacities are seen in the bilateral lung fields, likely representing mucoid impaction given known clinical history of cystic fibrosis. Prominent interstitial lung markings. 3.  Background parenchymal changes consistent with cystic fibrosis.

report:
NARRATIVE:
RADIOGRAPHIC EXAMINATION OF THE CHEST: September 2001
 
CLINICAL HISTORY:  age, Unknown, TRAUMA. Bicyclist involved in MVA. 
Reporting pain in the mid axillary line on the left.
 
COMPARISON: None.
 
PROCEDURE COMMENTS: Two views of the chest. 
 
FINDINGS:
 
Midline sternotomy wires are present with a broken superior most 
wire. A prosthetic aortic valve is in place. Suture material is noted 
in the left upper quadrant of the abdomen associated with elevation 
of the left hemidiaphragm. Stranding opacities are noted at the left 
base with blunting of the costophrenic sulcus. Apical pleural 
thickening is also noted on the left. The remainder of the lungs are 
otherwise clear. No evidence of pneumothorax. Mild cardiomegaly is 
noted. There is a suggestion of a tiny cortical step-off in the 
anterolateral aspect of the sixth left rib. No other obvious 
displaced rib fractures identified.
 
IMPRESSION:
 
1.  Findings in the left hemithorax including stranding opacities, 
small left pleural effusion likely related to old postsurgical 
changes given the presence of surgical material within the left upper 
quadrant of the abdomen. However, in the setting of the patient's 
mechanism of trauma, findings could be related to contusion and acute 
hemothorax, although no pneumothorax is identified. Recommend 
clinical correlation.
 
2.  Subtle cortical step-off along the anterolateral aspect of the 
left sixth rib is not well visualized given the overlying pulmonary 
findings. Correlate with physical exam for location of pain for 
possible underlying minimally displaced rib fracture.
 
3.  Mild cardiomegaly.
 
4.  Findings discussed with md lilliana jeremiah parsons emergency Department at 
4:40 PM.

spine.

CONSOLIDATION.

NARRATIVE:
RADIOGRAPHIC EXAMINATION OF THE CHEST: june 20th, 2017
 
CLINICAL HISTORY: 54 years of age, Male, R/o infiltrates. Patient has 
a history of heart transplant.
 
COMPARISON: Chest x-ray 6/20/2017 and CT scan JUNE 20, 2017
 
PROCEDURE COMMENTS: Two views of the chest. 
 
FINDINGS:
 
PA and lateral radiographs of the chest demonstrate similar 
postsurgical appearance of the chest and mediastinum, compatible with 
history of transplant. Multiple surgical fixators are seen across the 
anterior abdomen on the lateral radiograph, likely reflecting prior 
mesh hernia repair. Elevation of left hemidiaphragm is again seen 
with associated atelectasis or scarring, which has a slightly more 
nodular appearance on the current study. Bibasilar opacities, left 
greater than right, are again seen, similar compared to recent prior 
CT scan of 6/20/2017. The cardiomediastinal silhouette appears 
unchanged. Multiple old appearing rib fractures are seen on the 
right, similar compared to prior. Multilevel degenerative changes are 
also seen of the thoracic spine. No acute bony or soft tissue 
abnormalities are identified.
 
IMPRESSION:
 
1.  Similar postsurgical appearance of the chest and mediastinum.
 
2.  Similar appearing elevation of left hemidiaphragm with associated 
left basilar opacities which may reflect atelectasis, scarring, or 
consolidation.
 
3.  Haziness throughout the right lower lung zone is also again seen, 
and may reflect groundglass opacities, better evaluated on recent CT 
scan of 6-20-2017.

CHEST, ONE VIEW:  7-28-2000 
 
 CLINICAL HISTORY:  A 54-year-old man with a history of prednisone 
for 18 months, usual interstitial pneumonitis and a history of a 
large, over 2 cm right upper lobe pulmonary mass on CT from 
7/28/00.  
 
 FINDINGS:  This is an upright film in the recovery room which shows 
low lung volumes and bilateral interstitial linear findings 
compatible with a history of usual interstitial pneumonitis.  The 
irregular-shaped bilateral pulmonary nodules which, by report, had 
grown on outside CT scans are difficult to identify on this 
radiograph.  There is no definite pneumothorax on the current study.  
The largest pulmonary nodule that is still difficult to see is in the 
mid right lung, measuring 1.1 cm in size. 
 
 IMPRESSION: 
 
 1.  NO PNEUMOTHORAX ON RECOVERY ROOM FILM.  FINDINGS OF INTERSTITIAL 
LUNG DISEASE, LOW LUNG VOLUMES IS NOTED, AND THE PULMONARY NODULES 
ARE NOT AS EVIDENT AS THEY ARE ON THE PRIOR CT SCAN (SEE REPORT OF 
7-28-2000, UOI HIGH RESOLUTION CT). 
 
 SUMMARY:4-POSSIBLE SIGNIFICANT FINDINGS, MAY NEED ACTION.

hemidiaphragm with left lower lobe opacity and left pleural effusion.

line in stable position. Persistent barium is seen at the bilateral
lung bases.

interval repositioning of the nasogastric tube, now below the
gastroesophageal junction and off the inferior field of view.

its tip pointing superiorly. Placement of an endotracheal tube with
its tip approximately 5.5 cm above the carina. Otherwise, no
significant interval change.

placement of a right internal jugular Swan-Ganz catheter with its tip
within the region of the right ventricular outflow tract. Improved
aeration with decreasing left pleural effusion. Otherwise, no
significant interval change.
Follow-up chest x-ray done 06-03-13 at 0337 hours demonstrates
prominent lucency and at the left lower lung, likely colon. The right
internal jugular venous catheter may have been repositioned, however,
its tip is not well demonstrated on the current exam. Stable
cardiomediastinal silhouette. Otherwise, no significant interval
change.

RETROCARDIAC OPACIFICATION.
2. FEEDING TUBE COILED WITH ITS TIP POINTED SUPERIORLY WITHIN THE
STOMACH. NASOGASTRIC TUBE IN PLACE WITH ITS TIP BELOW THE
GASTROESOPHAGEAL JUNCTION BUT OFF THE INFERIOR FIELD OF VIEW. RIGHT

RECOMMEND CORRELATION CLINICALLY. ENDOTRACHEAL TUBE IN PLACE.

report:
NARRATIVE:
RADIOGRAPHIC EXAMINATION OF THE CHEST: 9-18-2020
 
CLINICAL HISTORY: 63 years of age, Female, Fall left posterior rib 
pain.
 
COMPARISON: None.
 
PROCEDURE COMMENTS: Two views of the chest. 
 
FINDINGS:
 
The mediastinal contour is normal. The heart is not enlarged, and the 
pulmonary vessels are not distended. There is mild blunting of the 
posterior costophrenic angles bilaterally. Biapical pleural scarring 
is also noted. There is no pneumothorax. There are linear opacities 
at the left lung base which may represent atelectasis or scarring. 
There is a subcentimeter nodular density projecting over the 
costochondral junction of the anterior right sixth rib likely 
representing costochondral calcification. No focal infiltrate or 
consolidation.
 
There is subtle cortical irregularity of the lateral margin of the 
left sixth rib concerning for fracture. There is an irregular 
sclerotic focus in the right humeral head with appearance of 
chondroid matrix corresponding to an area of increased uptake on 
prior bone scan of 9/18/2020, likely representing an enchondroma. The 
bones are diffusely undermineralized, and there are moderate 
multilevel degenerative changes in the spine.
 
IMPRESSION:
 
1.  Suspected minimally displaced fracture of the lateral left sixth 
rib. No pneumothorax. Osteoporosis limits detection of subtle 
fractures.
2.  Mild left basilar atelectasis or scarring.
3.  Mild blunting of the posterior costophrenic angles due to small 
pleural effusions or pleural scarring.
4.  Probable enchondroma in the proximal right humerus.

report:
NARRATIVE:
RADIOGRAPHIC EXAMINATION OF THE CHEST: 12/21/03
 
CLINICAL HISTORY: 65 years of age, Male, SOB, decreased left breath 
sounds. Patient has a history of rectal cancer, metastatic to the 
lungs.
 
COMPARISON: Chest x-ray 12-21-03 and CT scan 12/21/2003
 
PROCEDURE COMMENTS: Two views of the chest. 
 
FINDINGS:
 
PA and lateral radiographs of the chest demonstrate interval 
development of opacification throughout the majority of the left 
hemithorax with a small amount of residual aeration within the left 
upper lung zone likely reflecting a large pleural effusion. 
Additional airspace disease within the left lung cannot be excluded. 
Rounded opacity within the right upper lobe likely corresponds to the 
known nodule as seen on prior CT scan. There is rightward deviation 
of the trachea, suggestive of mass effect from the large pleural 
effusion. A tunneled right chest wall internal jugular Mediport is 
again seen. The right lung appears well aerated. Gaseous distention 
is seen of the esophagus. Multilevel degenerative changes are seen at 
the spine.
 
IMPRESSION:
 
1.  Interval development of near complete opacification of the left 
hemithorax with evidence of mass effect on the mediastinum with 
rightward deviation of the trachea. These findings are concerning for 
progression of the previously seen pleural effusion, now large in 
size. Superimposed airspace disease throughout the left mid and lower 
lung zone cannot be excluded including infection, aspiration, or 
progression of metastatic disease.
 
2.  The right lung appears fairly well aerated. The previously seen 
right pleural effusion appears decreased compared to prior. Rounded 
opacities within the right lung zone likely reflect known metastatic 
pulmonary nodules.
 
3.  Gaseous distention is seen of the esophagus.
 
4.  Unchanged appearance of right chest wall Mediport.
 
5.  These findings were discussed with nurse practitioner Aylin Villanueva by LE, JAMIE at 14:20 hours.

(Oncology At Harnett, Mhaf, Haematology).

comparison reveals again subpleural lower lobe prominent course 
reticular markings compatible with fibrotic changes.  The subpleural

unchanged.  There are no new other focal parenchymal opacities.

CHEST:  5-28-2003 
 
 COMPARISON:  None. 
 
 CLINICAL HISTORY:  A 65-year-old man with a history of 
hypersensitivity and pneumonitis, now with right lateral rib pain at 
the level of the nipple.  Chest x-ray to rule out pneumothorax. 
 
 FINDINGS:  Frontal and lateral views of the chest taken on 
5/28/2003 demonstrate normal cardiomediastinal silhouette.  Fine 
reticular opacities are seen in the lung with peripheral and basilar 
predominance.  They are particularly prominent on the lateral view at 
the posterior lungs.  Distribution is suggestive of pulmonary 
fibrosis.  Additional nodular patterns can be seen at the peripheral 
upper lungs.  While they most likely represent additional area of 
fibrosis, active pneumonitis cannot absolutely exclude it.  
Costophrenic sulci are sharp.  There is no evidence for pneumothorax.  
The ribs, where visualized, show no evidence of displaced fracture.  
There is evidence for osteopenia.  
 
 IMPRESSION: 
 
 1.  EVIDENCE FOR PULMONARY FIBROSIS, BUT CANNOT EXCLUDE ACUTE 
COMPONENTS OF PNEUMONITIS.  RECOMMEND COMPARISON WITH OUTSIDE OLD 
STUDY TO DEMONSTRATE ANY CHANGE. 
 
 2.  NO EVIDENCE FOR PNEUMOTHORAX AND NO DISPLACED RIB FRACTURE 
IDENTIFIED. 
 
 3.  RESULTS DISCUSSED WITH vance asher, md.  
 
 SUMMARY:4-POSSIBLE SIGNIFICANT FINDINGS, MAY NEED ACTION.
IMPRESSION:
The findings suggest lung fibrosis, in this particular distribution, 
most likely in a UIP pattern. Given the patient's history of 
hypersensitivity pneumonitis (fibrosis with chronic HP intends to 
involve more the upper lobes) however cannot be excluded.  A chest CT 
should be performed to better characterize the type of fibrosis.
END OF ADDENDUM:
 
SUMMARY:4-POSSIBLE SIGNIFICANT FINDINGS, MAY NEED ACTION
Addendum Ends

with atelectasis.

CLINICAL HISTORY: 61 years of age, Male, SOB found down; status post 
cardiac pulmonary resuscitation SOB.
 
COMPARISON: None.
 
PROCEDURE COMMENTS: Single AP view of the chest. 
 
FINDINGS:
 
There is a displaced fracture of the right posterior lateral seventh 
rib with associated moderate right pneumothorax. There is 
consolidation in the right lung near this region which may represent 
a pulmonary contusion. There is associated subcutaneous emphysema 
along the right lateral chest wall. In addition, on the left, there 
is consolidation at the left mid and lower lung zones with 
bronchograms. This area is suspicious for pneumonia. External pacer 
pads are present. An endotracheal tube has its tip just below the 
thoracic inlet. .
 
The heart is normal in size. The mediastinal contours are normal.     
 
IMPRESSION:
 
1.  Displaced right seventh rib fracture with associated moderate 
right apical and lateral pneumothorax and subcutaneous emphysema
 
2.  Adjacent pulmonary consolidation in the peripheral right midlung 
zone that may represent a contusion.
 
3.  Consolidation of the left mid and lower lung zones, probably 
pneumonia.
 
I discussed these results with rosanne, md on the following date and 
time: 7/3/2006 .

plugging reflecting cystic fibrosis nodular opacity in the left

ported central venous catheter remains in the right IJ vein with its 
tip in the upper right atrium.
 
IMPRESSION:
 
1.  Re-demonstration of changes of cystic fibrosis without new 
consolidation.

right internal jugular central venous catheter ends in the superior
vena cava.  There are two new right chest tubes, and a left chest
tube. There is no pneumothorax.  There is increased atelectasis at
both lung bases.  Heart remains enlarged.  Overall, however, the
pulmonary vasculature is less prominent consisting with some
resolution of previous pulmonary edema.  However, patchy pulmonary
opacities including the ill-defined nodular opacity in the right
middle lobe persist, although less well seen.  Aortic knob remains
enlarged with calcifications unchanged.

satisfactory positioning of all the tubes and lines.  Allowing for
differences in rotation there is no change in the cardiomediastinal
silhouette or pulmonary parenchyma.

MULTIPLE TUBES AND LINES AS DESCRIBED ABOVE DEMONSTRATING INCREASING
RETROCARDIAC CONSOLIDATION/ATELECTASIS BUT SLIGHTLY IMPROVED
PULMONARY VASCULAR PATTERN WITH DECREASED PULMONARY VESSEL DILATATION
COMPARED TO PREOPERATIVE FILMS.
 2.  CANNOT EXCLUDE SOME ELEMENT HOWEVER OF PERSISTENT INTERSTITIAL
CONGESTIVE HEART FAILURE.  LEFT LOWER LOBE CONSOLIDATION HAS
DEVELOPED POSTOPERATIVELY CONSISTENT WITH ATELECTASIS.
 SUMMARY:4-POSSIBLE SIGNIFICANT FINDINGS, MAY NEED ACTION

INTERVAL INCREASE IN INTERSTITIAL PULMONARY EDEMA AND DEVELOPMENT OF 
NEW OPACITIES WITHIN THE RIGHT UPPER LOBE AND RIGHT MIDDLE LOBE WITH 
PERSISTENT BASILAR OPACITIES.

CLINICAL HISTORY: 99 year old of age, Unknown, Trauma.
 
COMPARISON: None.
 
PROCEDURE COMMENTS: Single view of the chest. 
 
FINDINGS:
 
Patient is intubated with endotracheal tube tip 4.5 cm above the 
carina. Nasogastric tube extends below the edge of the radiograph. 
Prominent appearance of right hilum likely related to enlarged 
pulmonary vasculature. Cardiomediastinal silhouette appears mildly 
enlarged though not fully imaged on this portable chest radiograph 
limited due to trauma technique. Multiple right-sided rib fractures 
including the right third, fourth ribs.  Small right pleural 
effusion. No definite pneumothorax identified on this examination. 
Minimal opacity in the left retrocardiac region may represent 
atelectasis versus aspiration. Irregularity in the lateral third of 
the right clavicle concerning for clavicular fracture.
 
IMPRESSION:
 
1. Right clavicular fracture and right-sided rib fractures. No 
pneumothorax.
2. Intubation with endotracheal tube tip 4.5 cm above the carina.
3. Mild cardiomegaly with prominent pulmonary vasculature

apparatus is stable. With respect to the lung, there has been
interval increase in the coalescent opacities in the left lung and
the right perihilar region which can be consistent with contusion,
aspiration, and/or atelectasis. On the current film, there appears
to be increasing pulmonary edema.

radiographs versus CT, if one is performed. In addition, comparison
with old films would be helpful.

CHEST, ONE VIEW: 7/29/2015.

AP view of the chest.

None available.

superior mediastinum is markedly widened, the aortic arch appears
to be enlarged and in the area of the left apex. Without prior
images for comparisons, cannot evaluate the chronicity of these
findings. Recommend comparisons with prior films. There is mild
pulmonary edema. There is bibasilar consolidation, left greater
than right, which may represent atelectasis, cannot completely
exclude superimposed infection. Ill-defined 2 x 1.5 cm oval
lucency seen just to the left of the T4 vertebral body transverse
process, which may represent an area of aerated lung. There are
two figure of eight wires seen in the left lower lung zone, of
unclear etiology. Degenerative changes are seen at the
acromioclavicular joint, remaining bones and soft tissues are
unremarkable.

study compared to 8-27-14.

which may reflect a granuloma versus a sclerotic finding within the 
rib, or an object external to the patient. Attention is recommended 
on follow-up imaging.

TO RIGHT 10TH AND 11TH RIBS.

thoracic spine.  There is pleural effusion involving the bilateral 
hemithoraces, right greater than left.  There may also be a component 
of pleural thickening.

CAVITATION OF THE RIGHT UPPER LOBE.

RADIOGRAPHIC EXAMINATION OF THE CHEST: 9-14-2003 and chest 
x-ray 9/14/2003 at 20:22 hours
 
CLINICAL HISTORY: 73 years of age, Male, Eval pulm edema..
 
COMPARISON: Chest x-ray 9-14-03 and a chest x-ray 
9/14/2003 at 08:04 hours
 
PROCEDURE COMMENTS: Single view of the chest. 
 
FINDINGS:
 
On 9-14-2003 at 20:22 hours ((895) 506-4454) a single portable 
upright radiograph of the chest demonstrates bilateral low lung 
volumes, cardiomegaly, and increased pulmonary markings with 
bilateral parenchymal reticular opacification compatible with 
pulmonary edema. Blunting of bilateral costophrenic angles likely 
reflect small pleural effusions. No acute bony or soft tissue 
abnormalities are identified. A left PICC catheter tip projects 2.5 
cm below the level of the carina.
 
Subsequently on 9/14/2003 at 05:35 hours ((414) 390-2137) a single 
semiupright portable radiograph of the chest demonstrates persistent 
bilateral moderate to severe pulmonary edema. There is increasing 
focal opacity within the right perihilar region and right lateral 
lung. Bilateral pleural effusions are again seen. Persistent 
cardiomegaly. The bones and soft tissues appear unchanged.
 
IMPRESSION:
 
1.  Bilateral pulmonary edema which appears increasing compared to 
14 SEPTEMBER, now moderate to severe.
 
2.  Increasing focal opacity within the right perihilar and right 
lateral lung zones may reflect focal regions of atelectasis or 
consolidation if there is clinical concern for superimposed 
infection. Attention is recommended on follow-up imaging. 
 
3.  These findings were discussed with Averee Elizabeth Yang MD by Calhoun, Iris R at 
14:00 hours on 12/8/20.

report:
NARRATIVE:
RADIOGRAPHIC EXAMINATION OF THE CHEST: 12-8-13 at 4: 59 PM and 
12-8-2013
 
CLINICAL HISTORY: 40 years of age, Female, Post op.
 
COMPARISON: Chest x-ray december 8th, 2013 at 1:41 AM
 
PROCEDURE COMMENTS: Single view of the chest. 
 
FINDINGS:
 
12-8-2013 at 4:59 PM demonstrates interval placement of a 
nasogastric tube with tip in the stomach. Right IJ central line, left 
upper extremity PICC line, left IJ sheath, endotracheal tube, and 2 
left-sided chest tubes all appear stable in position. There is 
redemonstration of a surgical sponge in the left upper quadrant. This 
was communicated to the ICU team, who provided history that the 
patient has undergone splenectomy, and the abdomen remains open. 
Compared with the prior examination, the right-sided effusion has 
enlarged, and bilateral airspace opacities have become more 
confluent, especially on the right.
 
On 12-08 at 1:21 AM the nasogastric tube has been removed. 
There is a radiopaque tube projecting just to the right of the spine 
at the inferior aspect of the image. This is in an uncertain 
position. Other lines and tubes appear stable. The appearance of the 
chest continues to worsen with further enlargement of the right-sided 
effusion and more confluent air space opacities throughout the right 
lung and at the left base.
 
IMPRESSION:
 
1.  Progressive worsening in appearance of the chest with a large 
right-sided pleural effusion and confluent airspace opacities 
throughout the right lung and left lower lung.
 
2.  Surgical sponge in the left upper quadrant.
 
3.  Radiopaque tube projecting just to the right of the spine at the 
inferior aspect of the image. This is in an uncertain position, and 
may be external to the patient. Correlate clinically.
 
 
 
Physician to Physician Radiology Consult Line: (394) 743-2512

NARRATIVE:
RADIOGRAPHIC EXAMINATION OF THE CHEST: 6-5-2010
 
CLINICAL HISTORY: 67 years of age, Male, Post-op CV surgery.
 
COMPARISON: Chest radiograph 6-5-10
 
PROCEDURE COMMENTS: Single view of the chest. 
 
FINDINGS:
 
Chest radiograph 6/5/2010 at 17:40: Interval placement of median 
sternotomy wires, endotracheal tube terminating approximately 5 cm 
above the carina, enteric tube with the tip likely just past the 
gastroesophageal junction, right internal jugular central venous line 
with the tip at the cavoatrial junction, right internal jugular 
Swan-Ganz catheter in the main pulmonary trunk, 2 mediastinal drains, 
and left chest tube. Small left pleural effusion with left 
retrocardiac opacity, likely atelectasis. Interval resolution of the 
right pleural effusion and improvement in the right basilar opacity 
with likely residual bibasilar atelectasis.
 
Chest radiograph 6/5/2010 at 00:40: Interval repositioning of the 
enteric tube, which now coils in the stomach and courses back into 
the esophagus with the sidehole and tip in the mid esophagus directed 
superiorly. Slight interval retraction of the Swan-Ganz catheter, but 
it still remains in the main pulmonary trunk. The left chest tube 
appears to been repositioned such that the tip is now more medial 
compared to the prior radiograph. No other significant interval 
change.
 
Chest radiograph 6/5/2010 at 04:52: Slight advancement of the 
Swan-Ganz catheter, but it still remains in the main pulmonary trunk. 
Otherwise no significant interval change.
 
IMPRESSION:
 
1.  Interval placement of multiple lines and tubes as described.
 
2.  Enteric tube coils within the stomach and then courses back into 
the esophagus. The sidehole and tip of the tube are within the mid 
esophagus and are directed superiorly. Recommend repositioning.
 
3.  Small left pleural effusion with left retrocardiac opacity, 
likely reflecting atelectasis.
 
4.  Interval resolution of the right pleural effusion and improvement 
in the bibasilar opacity with likely residual right bibasilar 
atelectasis.
 
   
 
I have personally reviewed the images for this examination and agreed
with the report transcribed above.

report:
NARRATIVE:
PA AND LATERAL VIEWS OF THE CHEST:  09-02-01 
 
COMPARISON:  9/2/2001 and 9-2-2001.
 
CLINICAL HISTORY:  History of cough for one week.
 
FINDINGS:
Patchy, somewhat nodular consolidation is identified in the left 
perihilar region accentuated superiorly, as well as to a lesser 
degree in the mid to lower lungs, with a few tiny nodular densities 
in the right mid and lower lung currently apparent. (examination of 
9-2-2001 demonstrated a 14 mm nodule in the right lower lung, not 
noted on subsequent examination of 9/2/2001, with one of the 
currently noted nodular densities at approximately this location.)
 
Minor linear scarring versus atelectasis is seen medially in the 
right lower lung, diminished from prior study.  The lungs are 
otherwise clear with normal pulmonary vascularity.  
 
Cardiac size and configuration are within normal limits.  There is 
moderate elongation of the descending thoracic aorta, not 
significantly changed. 
 
Post-traumatic deformity of the left 5th rib is again noted.  There 
is evidence of prior vertebroplasty from level T11 inferiorly through 
L2, not significantly changed, with mild to moderate compression 
deformities of the bodies of T4, T6, T8, and T10 again identified, 
age indeterminate.  
 
There is relative sclerosis of the spinous process of T1, not 
significantly changed from CT examination of 6/1/2019, with that 
examination demonstrating heterogeneous appearance of the bones 
diffusely, with areas of lucency and sclerosis, likely relating to 
the patient's reported myeloma.  
 
IMPRESSION:
 
PATCHY BILATERAL, SOMEWHAT NODULAR PULMONARY CONSOLIDATION, 
ACCENTUATED IN THE LEFT PERIHILAR REGION, POSSIBLY INFECTIOUS IN 
ETIOLOGY.  FOLLOW-UP CHEST RADIOGRAPHIC EXAMINATION WOULD BE HELPFUL 
IN FURTHER EVALUATION. 
 
SUMMARY:4-POSSIBLE SIGNIFICANT FINDINGS, MAY NEED ACTION

a similar appearance. Recommend clinical correlation.

inferior edge of today's film.  A right-sided PICC line is seen with
distal tip at the distal aspect of the superior vena cava.

SMALL NODULAR OPACITIES AT THE RIGHT UPPER LUNG AND PERSISTENT SMALL
RIGHT PLEURAL EFFUSION.
 2.  RIGHT-SIDED PICC LINE, UNCHANGED.
 3.  PATIENT IS STATUS POST DOUBLE LUNG TRANSPLANTATION WITH
POSTSURGICAL CHANGES AGAIN SEEN.
 SUMMARY:2-ABNORMAL, PREVIOUSLY REPORTED

TWO VIEWS OF THE CHEST:   September 09

transplant presenting for follow-up evaluation.  
 
 FINDINGS:   The heart size is within normal limits.  Redemonstration 
of post-surgical changes in the mediastinum consistent with prior 
lung transplantation.  There has been interval development of patchy 
air-space opacities within the right mid to lower lung zone which 
appear localized to the right middle lobe on the lateral projection.  
The findings are concerning for possible developing consolidation.  
Elsewhere, there is redemonstration of multiple small nodular 
opacities primarily within the right upper lung zone which are stable 
compared to the prior study.  There is redemonstration of bilateral 
apical pleural parenchymal thickening which is unchanged.  
 
 IMPRESSION:  
 
 1.  DEMONSTRATION OF NEW PATCHY AIR-SPACE OPACITIES WITHIN THE RIGHT 
MIDDLE LOBE CONCERNING FOR DEVELOPING CONSOLIDATION OR INFECTION.  
 
 SUMMARY:4-POSSIBLE SIGNIFICANT FINDINGS, MAY NEED ACTION

report:
NARRATIVE:
HISTORY:
A 79-year-old woman with history of breast cancer and pulmonary
hypertension. Recent desaturation. The patient is obtaining a V/Q
scan on the same day today.
CHEST, PORTABLE SEMIUPRIGHT AP, 11/19/2018:
The heart is enlarged, as is the main pulmonary artery . No
definite pulmonary edema is identified. There is interstitial
thickening, which could be better evaluated with a CT scan. A
small right pleural effusion and a slightly larger left pleural
effusion are identified. Bilateral axillary clips are seen,
representing bilateral axillary node dissection.
CHEST, PORTABLE UPRIGHT AP, 11/19/2018:
There has been no significant interval change, given the slight
differences in positioning.
CHEST CT: 11-19-2018
TECHNIQUE:
Contiguous helical axial images were obtained through the thorax
without intravenous contrast due to the patient's heart and renal
failure.
FINDINGS:
The main pulmonary artery is severely enlarged to 3.7 cm, with
enlargement of the right main pulmonary artery (2.2 cm) and left
(2.0 cm), consistent with pulmonary hypertension. The ascending
aorta measures 3.2 cm. There is biventricular and right atrial
enlargement. A small pericardial effusion is seen with no
pericardial calcifications. The intrahepatic inferior vena cava is
enlarged.
Lung windows demonstrate diffuse interlobular septal thickening,
predominantly at the lower lung zones. Mild cylindrical
bronchiectasis is identified in the right lower lobe. There is
mild diffuse patchy ground-glass opacification, predominantly in
the lower zones.
Biapical pleuro-parenchymal thickening is seen, left greater than
right, with architectural distortion of the left apex and traction
bronchiectasis. Slightly nodular appearance is seen in the area of
the thickening in the right apex.
A 4 mm, noncalcified, spiculated nodule is seen at the right lung
apex, not contiguous with the pleura (series 3, image 37). A
calcified granuloma is identified at the right lung base.
Moderate, layering bilateral pleural effusions are identified, with
associated compressive atelectasis of the posterior portions of the
lower lobes.
A 9 mm, right paratracheal lymph node is seen, not meeting CT
criteria for enlargement. A 1.1 cm, enlarged lymph node is seen in
the right pretracheal region. The patient has had bilateral
mastectomies, and clips from prior lymph node dissection are seen
in both axillae.
The upper abdomen demonstrates calcified atherosclerosis of the
aorta, including thick calcifications at the origins of the celiac
axis and bilateral renal arteries. The kidneys demonstrate
residual contrast in the cortex without evidence of contrast
excretion. Bone windows demonstrate no lytic or blastic lesions to
suggest metastatic disease. Degenerative disc disease is
identified in the mid and lower thoracic spine.
IMPRESSION:
1. INTERSTITIAL THICKENING WITH BILATERAL PLEURAL EFFUSIONS. WITH
THE HISTORY OF BREAST CANCER, COULD REPRESENT LYMPHANGITIC SPREAD
OF CARCINOMA. HOWEVER, CHF WITH PULMONARY EDEMA CAN HAVE A SIMILAR
APPEARANCE.
2. SEVERE PULMONARY HYPERTENSION, LIKELY SECONDARY TO LEFT
VENTRICULAR FAILURE.
3. BILATERAL PLEURAL EFFUSIONS WITH ASSOCIATED BIBASILAR
ATELECTASIS.
4. SPICULATED PULMONARY NODULE AT THE RIGHT APEX. COMPARISON WITH
PRIOR STUDIES OR FOLLOW-UP WOULD BE RECOMMENDED TO ASSESS
STABILITY.
5. BIAPICAL FIBROSIS, LIKELY REPRESENTING SCARRING. A NODULAR
COMPONENT AT THE RIGHT APEX IS SEEN, WHERE MALIGNANCY CANNOT BE
EXCLUDED. AGAIN, COMPARISON WITH PRIOR STUDIES OR FOLLOW-UP IS
RECOMMENDED TO ASSESS FOR STABILITY.
6. RESIDUAL CONTRAST IN THE RENAL CORTICES, LIKELY FROM A PRIOR
CONTRAST-ENHANCED IMAGING STUDY, WITHOUT EXCRETION, ACUTE VS
CHRONIC RENAL FAILURE.
END OF IMPRESSION:
SUMMARY 4: Possible significant abnormality/change, may need
action.

report:
NARRATIVE:
PA AND LATERAL CHEST:  8/27/2011.
 
CLINICAL DATA:  A 77-year-old male with history of left-sided rib 
pain after fall three weeks ago.  
 
COMPARISON:  None.
 
FINDINGS:  Cardiomediastinal silhouette demonstrates slightly 
enlarged aortic arch shadow measuring up to 5 cm in size.  The 
pulmonary arteries are unremarkable.  No evidence of lymphadenopathy 
is noted within the mediastinum. Heart shadow is unremarkable.  
 
There is symmetric apical pleural thickening.  No pleural effusion is 
noted.  However, the left costophrenic angle is not fully included. 
No pneumothorax.
 
A 6 mm, well-circumscribed nodular opacity is seen in the right upper 
lung zone.  No other air space opacity is seen.  
 
Deformity of the right fifth rib is present, suggesting prior 
fracture.  No evidence of acute fracture is identified on the left. 
No callous deposition could be clearly seen.  
 
Likely DISH of the thoracic spine.
IMPRESSION: 
 
1.  NO DEFINITE LEFT RIB FRACTURE IS IDENTIFIED.  HOWEVER, THE LOWER 
RIBS ARE NOT FULLY INCLUDED ON THE PRESENT STUDY. 
 
2.  AORTIC ARCH MEASURES UP TO 5 CM IN SIZE.  RECOMMEND FURTHER 
ASSESSMENT WITH EITHER ECHOCARDIOGRAM OR POSSIBLY CT ANGIO OF THE 
CHEST FOR BETTER CHARACTERIZATION.  
 
3.  A 6 MM ROUNDED NODULE OF THE RIGHT UPPER LUNG ZONE, WHICH COULD 
REPRESENT A GRANULOMA. IF PRIOR FILMS ARE AVAILABLE, COMPARISON COULD 
HELP ESTABLISH STABILITY.  IF NOT, FURTHER EVALUATION WITH CT OF THE 
CHEST CAN BE CONSIDERED IF CLINICALLY INDICATED.  
 
SUMMARY:4-POSSIBLE SIGNIFICANT FINDINGS, MAY NEED ACTION

cystic fibrosis.

the setting of hypoplastic right lung or Scimitar syndrome.  CT chest 
with contrast may be obtained for confirmation.

lung apices, which may be due to mucous plugging and superimposed 
infection.
 
Normal heart size and pulmonary vascularity.
 
No pleural effusion or pneumothorax.  Bones are unremarkable.
 
 
SUMMARY:4-POSSIBLY SIGNIFICANT FINDING, MAY NEED ACTION

apical pleural thickening and a pleural-based mass in the left 
midlung, but no associated bony destruction. Minimal retrocardiac 
opacification and likely small left pleural effusion.
 
2.  Small nodular densities in the right apical region on the right 
base.

NARRATIVE:
RADIOGRAPHIC EXAMINATION OF THE CHEST POST NEEDLE BIOPSY: 00, july 30
 
CLINICAL HISTORY: 73 years of age, Female, S/p left T6-8 intercostal 
nerve block and alcohol neurolysis.
 
COMPARISON: CT scan of the chest 7/30/2000 and chest x-ray 
7/30/2000
 
PROCEDURE COMMENTS: Single view of the chest. 
 
FINDINGS:
 
Single portable semiupright radiograph of the chest demonstrates 
multiple ill-defined patchy opacities throughout the bilateral lung 
zones, as well as increased reticular markings bilaterally, likely 
reflecting the multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules as seen on prior 
CT scan as well as mild pulmonary edema versus lymphangitic spread of 
disease. Left greater than right pleural thickening is again seen, 
which may reflect extrapleural soft tissue versus pleural effusions. 
The large pleural-based left mid lung zone nodule is better seen on 
prior CT scan. Small amount of extra lucency is seen along the left 
lateral cardiac silhouette, which may reflect overlapping shadows 
versus a small amount of gas within the mediastinum. Rightward 
deviation of the trachea is again seen, compatible with large thyroid 
nodule as seen on prior CT scan. Postsurgical changes compatible with 
history of left lower lobectomy. The multiple left-sided rib 
fractures are better evaluated on the prior CT scan.
 
IMPRESSION:
 
1.  Multiple bilateral ill-defined patchy opacities appear similar 
compared to prior CT scan, compatible with history of metastatic 
disease. Increased interstitial markings may reflect new pulmonary 
edema versus lymphangitic spread of disease.
 
2.  Increased blunting of bilateral costophrenic angles and pleural 
thickening is again seen which may reflect increased extrapleural 
soft tissues versus new pleural effusions.
 
3.  A small amount of extra lucency is seen along the left lateral 
cardiac silhouette, which may reflect overlapping shadows versus a 
tiny amount of pneumomediastinum in the setting of recent intercostal 
nerve block.
 
4.  The large pleural-based left midlung zone nodule is better seen 
on prior CT scan, as are the multiple left-sided rib fractures.
 
5.  Rightward deviation of the trachea is again seen compatible with 
large thyroid nodule.

and placement of a large bore pleural drain with its tip abutting the

previously 27 mm. There is a persistent fluid component to the left 
hydropneumothorax predominantly in the inferior left hemithorax.

fullness along the left margin reflecting underlying mediastinal 
mass.

persistent small left hydropneumothorax with 14 mm of pleural 
retraction of the apical gaseous component. There is interval 
decrease in the fluid component in the inferior left hemithorax 
though there is trace left pleural fluid remaining. No other 
significant change.
 
IMPRESSION:
 
1. Interval removal of a pigtail pleural drain from the left chest 
cavity and placement of a large-bore left chest tube with interval 
decrease in size of the left hydropneumothorax, as described.

report:
NARRATIVE:
RADIOGRAPHIC EXAMINATION OF THE ABDOMEN: 6/21/16
 
CLINICAL HISTORY: 19 years of age, Male, NG placement.
 
COMPARISON: Radiograph from one day prior
 
PROCEDURE COMMENTS:
Single view of the chest.
 Single view of the abdomen.
 
FINDINGS:
 
Single view of the chest:
 
The right sided central venous access port terminates in the cavoatrial junction. The left arm PICC line terminates in the right atrium. An NG/OG tube courses below the diaphragm and out of the inferior field of view. The endotracheal tube terminates in the mid trachea at the level of T2. There is redemonstration of sternotomy wires.
 
There is similar appearance of the large collection versus mass in the inferior left hemithorax, unchanged since the comparison. There is redemonstration of left pleural nodularity and associated left pleural effusion. There is continued interval improvement in pulmonary edema. There is a small right pleural effusion and patchy opacification in the right lung base and left upper lobe.
 
There is mild rightward the external shift, unchanged. Evaluation of heart size is limited by obscuration of the left heart border by the adjacent collection.
 
No acute bony abnormalities are noted.
 
Single view the abdomen:
 
The film is rotated and the inferior abdomen/pelvis is not included. The NG/OG tube terminates in the distal stomach. The stomach bubble is displaced inferiorly and medially, possibly due to increase in size of the known fluid collection versus cystic mass in the inferior left hemithorax. There are mildly dilated stacking small bowel loops in the lower abdomen. The films do not include the rectum to evaluate for distal gas. Stool is noted in the ascending colon. There is no pneumatosis or portal venous gas seen. There is no evidence of pneumoperitoneum on this supine film.
 
 IMPRESSION:
 
1.  Stable large cystic mass in the left inferior pneumothorax and left abdomen.
 
2.  Redemonstration of left pleural nodularity and associated left pleural effusion.
 
3.  Persistent small right pleural effusion and atelectasis of the right lung base.
 
4.  Continued interval improvement in pulmonary edema.
 
5.  The NG/OG tube terminates in the distal stomach.
 
6.  Medial and inferior displacement of the stomach bubble, due to mass effect from soft tissue density mass in the left upper quadrant/inferior left hemithorax. This appears increased relative to the CT scout from 6-21-2016, possibly due to interval growth in the large cystic mass.
 
7.  Gaseous dilatation of the small bowel may represent ileus. If associated abdominal pain and concern for obstruction, consider dedicated abdominal radiograph to fully evaluate the bowel.

report:
NARRATIVE:
EXAM: Chest 1 View, 3/12/2014
 
CLINICAL HISTORY: Postop
 
COMPARISON: 03/12/14
 
FINDINGS: 
 
Single frontal view of chest on 3/12/2014 1809: New endotracheal tube 
with tip 8 cm above the level of the carina and new temperature 
probe, with tip overlying the upper esophagus..  Left upper extremity 
PICC again appears looped over the left subclavian vein.  Interval 
removal of feeding tube and right internal jugular line and placement 
of a nasogastric tube with tip below the inferior margin of film. Two 
new left internal jugular lines are seen come with tips overlying the 
left internal jugular vein. Stable left pleural pigtail drain.  New 
drain over the right upper quadrant.  Stable small bilateral pleural 
effusions.  Stable confluent airspace opacity in the retrocardiac 
region.  Mild pulmonary edema.
 
Single frontal view of chest on 12-3 12043: Interval removal of 
temperature probe. Other support hardware appear unchanged in 
position.  Stable confluent airspace opacity in the left lung base 
and small bilateral pleural effusions.  No pulmonary edema or 
pneumothorax.  Stable cardiomegaly.
 
Single frontal view chest on 03/12/14 at 0506: Endotracheal tube tip is 
7 cm above the carina.  Stable position of other support hardware.  
Stable confluent left retrocardiac airspace opacity.  Stable small 
left pleural effusion.  Stable slightly increased small right pleural 
effusion.  Stable mild pulmonary edema.  No pneumothorax.
 
 
IMPRESSION:
 
1.SERIES OF 3 FRONTAL CHEST RADIOGRAPHS DEMONSTRATES NEW HARDWARE, 
INCLUDING ENDOTRACHEAL TUBE WITH TIP 7-8 CM ABOVE THE CARINA, NEW 
NASOGASTRIC TUBE, AND TWO NEW LEFT INTERNAL JUGULAR LINES.  NEW DRAIN 
OVERLIES RIGHT UPPER QUADRANT.  LEFT UPPER EXTREMITY PICC AGAIN 
APPEARS LOOPED OVER THE LEFT BRACHIOCEPHALIC VEIN.  THESE FINDINGS 
WERE DISCUSSED WITH THE SICU TEAM ON 3-12-2014 AT 9:30 A.M.
 
2.STABLE SMALL BILATERAL PLEURAL EFFUSIONS AND MILD PULMONARY EDEMA.
 
3.STABLE CONFLUENT AIRSPACE OPACITY IN THE LUNG BASES, LEFT GREATER 
THAN RIGHT.  NO PNEUMOTHORAX.
 
 
SUMMARY:4-POSSIBLY SIGNIFICANT FINDING, MAY NEED ACTION

report:
NARRATIVE:
RADIOGRAPHIC EXAMINATION OF THE CHEST:3/9/08 at 15:51 hours 
and 23:48 hours
And 08/9 at 04:04 hours and 10:24 hours
 
CLINICAL HISTORY: 36 years of age, Male, Evaluation for organ 
donation..
 
COMPARISON: 2008, March 9 at 10:48 hours
 
PROCEDURE COMMENTS: Single view of the chest. 
 
FINDINGS:
3-9-08 at 15:51 hours shows a 5 cm left apical 
pneumothorax, moderate in size, unchanged from the previous study. 
Bilateral patchy airspace opacities in the upper left lung 
representing probable contusion or hemorrhage are stable. Left rib 
fractures are unchanged. There are still bilateral chest tubes and 
right pleural fluid. The upper left central line still terminates in 
the superior vena cava. There is an endotracheal tube in place. There 
is an NG tube with its tip in the stomach. No change in the right 
clavicular fracture
 
March 2008 at 23:48 hours shows increasing opacities at the 
lung bases, slightly enlarged heart and increasing pleural fluid 
collections. The left apical pneumothorax now measures 3.1 cm in 
size. There is no other change. 
 
 3/9/2008 hours Supporting medical devices and drains are 
unchanged since the prior study in the left apical pneumothorax now 
measures 5.6 cm in size. The 2.4 sq cm opacity projected over the 
lower chest/upper abdomen is again seen, previously also seen on the 
3/9/2008 study.. 
 
3-9-2008 hours hours shows that the radiopaque device 
projecting over the spine has been removed, and was external to the 
patient. The apical pneumothorax on the left still measures 5 cm on 
the last study. There is no other change except for partial clearing 
of the left basilar opacities.
 
IMPRESSION:
 
5 cm left apical pneumothorax persists  on the last study.
 
Patchy opacity in the left upper lobe noted.
 
Bilateral lower lobe opacities, right greater than left; on the last 
study bilateral pleural fluid collections are noted.    
 
No change in right clavicular and left rib fractures 
 
"Physician to Physician Radiology Consult Line: (775) 609-1584"

chest tube with resolution of the right-sided pneumothorax. Extensive 
soft tissue emphysema and no mediastinal emphysema is again noted.

in correct position. All of the supporting devices and chest tubes 
are in unchanged positions. No pneumothorax. Readily decreasing soft 
tissue emphysema.
 
10/30/2013, at 22:02 hours: Interval redevelopment of the right-sided 
pneumothorax, despite unchanged position of all chest tubes and other 
supporting devices. Worsening soft tissue emphysema.
 
October 2013, at 22:33 hours: Interval repositioning of the right chest 
tube and placement of a second right chest tube with resolution of 
the pneumothorax. Other supporting devices remain on changed in 
correct positions. Stable soft tissue emphysema and cardiopulmonary

pneumothorax with well expanded right lung. Stable mild edema.

the mid esophagus and should be advanced. ET tube, right IJ line,

all unchanged. No pneumothorax. Gradually decreasing soft tissue 
emphysema. No cardiopulmonary status with persistent mild edema.

of the right-sided pneumothorax, with resolution after placement of 2 
chest tubes.

interval removal of the more superiorly placed right-sided thoracic

coiling material and staples project over the upper abdomen.

zone, concerning for aspiration versus infection. Persistent mild 
pulmonary edema. Small bilateral pleural effusions. The cardiac 
silhouette is within normal limits.

new small right pneumothorax.

increased left pneumothorax and decreased right pneumothorax. 
Increased mild pulmonary edema.
 
IMPRESSION:
 
1. Interval removal of a right-sided thoracic drain with development 
of a small right pneumothorax with subsequent decrease in size.
 
2. Interval enlargement of a small left pneumothorax.
 
3. Increased mild pulmonary edema.

11/26
 
CLINICAL HISTORY: 60 years of age, Female, Every morning while 
intubated.

worsening ARDS. Persistent small left apical pneumothorax.

airspace opacities concerning for worsening ARDS.
 
2.  Removal of 1 of the 2 left pleural drains with development of a 
small left apical pneumothorax.

resolution of the previously seen small apical pneumothorax. Pleural 
thickening is seen along the left lateral chest wall, with unchanged 
patchy opacification of the left base.

NARRATIVE:
EXAM: Chest 1 View, 7-26-17
 
CLINICAL HISTORY: 82-year-old female R IJ, PA catheter.
 
COMPARISON: 7/26/2017, 7/26/2017
 
FINDINGS:
 
On a frontal chest x-ray obtained 7-26-17 at 4:41 a.m., ET tube, 
left internal jugular central line, rib plates and sternal plates, 
dual lead pacemaker, and right axilla surgical clips appear unchanged 
in position. The nasogastric tube extends passing through margin of 
the study and the previously seen coiling of the nasogastric tube in 
the hypopharynx cannot evaluated in this study as the hypopharynx is 
not included in the field-of-view.  There is interval development of 
a large right pneumothorax with partial collapse of the right lung.  
Otherwise there is stable mild cardiomegaly, trace pulmonary edema, 
and bilateral pleural effusions appear mildly improved.
 
On a subsequent frontal chest x-ray obtained 7/26/2017 at 6:07 a.m., 
there has been interval placement of a right chest tube with near 
complete resolution of the right pneumothorax.  There are no other 
interval changes.
 
Frontal chest x-ray obtained 7/26/17 at 7:17 a.m. shows interval 
placement of a right internal jugular Schwann Ganz catheter with its 
tip seen in the right main pulmonary artery.  There is no interval 
change in the positioning of the other lines, tubes or devices.  
There is no interval change in the cardia pulmonary status.
 
IMPRESSION:
 
1.THERE WAS INTERVAL DEVELOPMENT OF A LARGE RIGHT PNEUMOTHORAX WHICH 
SUBSEQUENTLY RESOLVED AFTER PLACEMENT OF A RIGHT CHEST TUBE.  THERE 
IS INTERVAL PLACEMENT OF A RIGHT INTERNAL JUGULAR SCHWANN GANZ 
CATHETER WITH ITS TIP SEEN IN THE RIGHT MAIN PULMONARY ARTERY.  ET 
TUBE, NASOGASTRIC TUBE, LEFT INTERNAL JUGULAR CENTRAL LINE,  RIB 
PLATES AND STERNAL PLATES, DUAL LEAD PACEMAKER, AND RIGHT AXILLA 
SURGICAL CLIPS APPEAR UNCHANGED.
 
2.THERE IS STABLE MILD CARDIOMEGALY, TRACE PULMONARY EDEMA, AND MILD 
IMPROVEMENT OF THE BILATERAL PLEURAL EFFUSIONS.

RADIOGRAPHIC EXAMINATIONS OF THE CHEST: 7/11/2013
 
CLINICAL HISTORY: 53 years of age, Male, Post op.
 
COMPARISON: 2013-7-11
 
PROCEDURE COMMENTS: Single views of the chest at 2342 hours July 2013, 0115 hours 7/11/2013 and 0540 hours 07-11-13. 
 
FINDINGS:
 
AP semisupine chest radiograph at 2342 hours demonstrates interval 
median sternotomy, with a prosthetic valve replacement and intact 
sternal wires. The patient is intubated, with the tip of the ET tube 
4.3 cm above the carina. A nasogastric tube is seen with the tip not 
clearly visualized. A right subclavian Swan-Ganz catheter is present, 
with the tip in the main pulmonary outflow tract. There is also a 
right subclavian venous line. A surgical drain projects over the 
mediastinum. An AICD device is in unchanged position. The patient is 
markedly rotated. Prominent band atelectasis is seen at the left 
base, with a likely small pleural effusion. The right lung base is 
not clearly seen.
 
AP supine chest radiograph at 0115 hours 7-11-13 demonstrates 
stable position of lines and tubes. Lung volumes are low, with 
improving band atelectasis at the left base. There is also 
opacification of the right base, with a small layering pleural 
effusion. A small calcified granuloma is now seen in the right 
midlung peripherally.
 
AP supine chest radiograph at 0540 hours 7/11/13 again 
demonstrates stable position of lines and tubes. Improved aeration is 
seen at the right base compared to prior, with the small right 
pleural effusion. Persistent band atelectasis is seen at the left 
base.
 
IMPRESSION:
 
1.  Post sternotomy changes, with a prosthetic cardiac valve.
 
2.  Right basal opacification and layering right pleural effusion, 
improving on subsequent radiographs.
 
3.  Improving basilar atelectasis at the left base.

is again shown, suspicious for an infectious process. There is also a 
new airspace opacity projecting on the right hilum, which most likely 
corresponds to the focal consolidation in the superior segment of the 
right lower lobe seen on a recent CT scan. The remainder of the lung 
fields remain clear. Heart size is mildly enlarged.

redemonstration of a right superior segment of the lower lobe 
airspace disease, these opacities most likely represent infection and 
are compatible with fungal disease.
 
IMPRESSION:
 
1.  Serial radiographs show likely multifocal fungal pneumonia in the 
right upper lobe and in the superior segment of the right lower lobe.

NARRATIVE:
RADIOGRAPHS OF THE WRIST, SHOULDER, AND CHEST: 7/6/14
 
CLINICAL HISTORY: 115 year old of age, Female, R/o rib fracture. Shoulder 
pain. Wrist pain.
 
COMPARISON: Chest radiograph on 7/2014
 
PROCEDURE COMMENTS: Single view of the chest. 4 views of the left 
shoulder. 3 views of the left wrist.
 
FINDINGS:
 
Chest radiograph: There is a 2-lead cardiac pacemaker. There are 
surgical clips along the right upper quadrant of the abdomen. 
Nondisplaced rib fracture in the posterior lateral left ninth rib. 
Unchanged appearance of right apical opacification with pleural 
parenchymal scarring. Bilateral reticulation, likely related to 
chronic lung disease. Small 1.5 cm rounded nodular opacity in the 
right upper lobe appears new from prior in 11-12-2001. Calcified aorta.
 
Left shoulder: Fracture of the left humeral head, with minimal 
displacement of the fragment laterally, and with mild impaction. No 
dislocation. No additional fractures visible.
 
Left wrist: Mild widening of the scapholunate joint. No visible 
fracture. Degenerative change of the first CMC joint.
 
IMPRESSION:
 
1.  Left shoulder: Left humeral head fracture. 
 
2.  Chest: Nondisplaced rib fracture in the posterior lateral ninth 
rib on the left. Unchanged pleural parenchymal scarring at the right 
lung apex. Small 1.5 cm rounded nodular opacity in the right upper 
lobe appears new from prior in 11/12/01. Consider non-urgent outpatient 
CT thorax for further evaluation if clinically appropriate.
 
3.  Left wrist: Mild widening of the scapholunate joint, which can 
reflect ligamentous injury. No acute fracture. If there is a clinical 
concern for scaphoid fracture, we recommend repeat radiographs in 
7-10 days as acute fractures may be radiographically occult.

with the report transcribed above.

 COMPARISON:   8/31/03.   
 
 FINDINGS:   
 
 Single frontal view of the chest obtained 8-31-03 at 1250 
hours demonstrates stable positioning of the left anterior chest wall 
pacemaker.   Redemonstration of elevation of the right hemidiaphragm, 
as well as mild vascular indistinctness which may represent mild 
pulmonary edema.   There is slight prominence of the right perihilar 
region.   No other focal consolidations or significant pleural 
effusions.  
 
 Subsequent single frontal view of the chest obtained AUGUST 31ST, 2003 
at 1707 hours demonstrates interval intubation with the tip of the 
endotracheal tube projecting 5.2 cm above the carina.  Interval 
development of alveolar opacities in the right mid lung zone, 
concerning for infection.   A new dense retrocardiac opacity is also 
present.   
 
 Subsequent single frontal view of the chest obtained 8/31/2003 
at 1911 hours demonstrates interval placement of a nasogastric tube 
which extends below the diaphragm and beyond the inferior margin of 
the film.  Remaining support equipment appears stable.  Interval 
progression of diffuse alveolar opacities in the right lung.  The 
left lung remains clear.   
 
 IMPRESSION:  
 
 1.  SERIES OF THREE CHEST RADIOGRAPHS DEMONSTRATE INTERVAL 
INTUBATION AND PLACEMENT OF SUPPORT EQUIPMENT, AS DESCRIBED ABOVE.  
 
 2.  INTERVAL DEVELOPMENT OF DIFFUSE ALVEOLAR OPACITIES WITHIN THE 
RIGHT LUNG, CONCERNING FOR INFECTION.  DENSE RETROCARDIAC OPACITY MAY 
REPRESENT ATELECTASIS VERSUS CONSOLIDATION.  
 
 SUMMARY: 4-POSSIBLE SIGNIFICANT FINDINGS, MAY NEED ACTION

CLINICAL HISTORY: 81 years of age, Female, Intubation, CVC placement.
 
COMPARISON: 10-22-2009
 
PROCEDURE COMMENTS: Single view of the chest. 
 
FINDINGS:
 
Single supine portable frontal view of the chest demonstrates an 
endotracheal tube in place, with tip at the carina. A right internal 
jugular central venous sheath is present, with tip in the proximal 
SVC. Nasogastric tube is present, with tip below the left 
hemidiaphragm and below the confines of the film. Thoracolumbar 
spinal hardware is in place. Lung volumes are low. There is a 
possible left pleural effusion with associated minimal retrocardiac 
opacity, likely atelectasis. No pneumothorax. Degenerative changes of 
the right shoulder, partially visualized.
 
IMPRESSION:
 
1.  Interval placement of thoracolumbar spinal hardware to correct 
scoliosis.
 
2.  Endotracheal tube tip at the carina. Recommend retraction x 3.5 
cm. Findings discussed with zariah stewart, dr. in the ICU at 10:05 AM on 
10/22/2009.
 
3.  Low lung volumes with possible small left pleural effusion and 
minimal left base atelectasis.

CHEST, TWO VIEWS: 8/1/2002.
COMPARISON: No prior studies for comparison.
CLINICAL DATA: 96 year old female with shortness of breath. Rule
out pneumonia.
FINDINGS:
The cardiomediastinal size and configuration are within normal
limits. There is demonstration of increased opacity in the
retrocardiac left lower lobe, suggestive of either atelectasis or
a consolidative process such as pneumonia. Additionally, strandy
opacity is seen at the right lung base that is favored to represent
atelectasis. The pulmonary vascularity is within normal limits.
No pneumothorax is identified. There is demonstration of anterior
loss of height of one of the vertebral bodies in the mid thorax, of
unknown acuity. Please correlate clinically.
IMPRESSION:
1. INCREASED OPACITY IN THE LEFT LOWER LOBE AND AT THE RIGHT LUNG
BASE. FINDINGS MAY BE SECONDARY TO ATELECTASIS, ALTHOUGH A
CONSOLIDATIVE PROCESS SUCH AS PNEUMONIA CANNOT BE EXCLUDED IN THE
LEFT LOWER LOBE. A DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSTIC CONSIDERATION FOR THESE
FINDINGS WOULD BE ASPIRATION.
2. COMPRESSION DEFORMITY OF A MID THORACIC VERTEBRAL BODY, OF
UNCERTAIN ACUITY. PLEASE CORRELATE CLINICALLY.

action.
